record.context_brief: finite-sample KL risk for exponential-family MLE and MAP
record.original_question: Let p(· | θ*) be a well-specified exponential-family distribution, let T(X) be its sufficient statistic, let μ* = E_{θ*}[T(X)] be the mean parameter, and let D_n = (X_1, …, X_n) be iid samples. The maximum-likelihood estimator uses the empirical mean (1/n) ∑_i T_i, while the conjugate maximum a posteriori estimator with prior hyperparameters (n_0, μ_0) uses (n_0μ_0 + ∑_i T_i)/(n_0 + n). Find non-asymptotic upper bounds, valid for finite sample size n and for a broad class of exponential families including small-sample regimes, for the frequentist risk measured by the expected Kullback-Leibler divergence from the true model to these estimators, equivalently the expected Bregman divergence BA*(μ*; (1/n) ∑_i T_i) for MLE and BA*(μ*; (n_0μ_0 + ∑_i T_i)/(n_0 + n)) for MAP, where the final upper bounds should not themselves leave an expectation over the dataset.

evidence.quote: Find an upper bound on the expected value of KL(pθ* ||pθ̂MLE/MAP_n) .

Open Problem 1 (Upper-bounding MAP and MLE). Upper bound the following quantities: MLE: E_Dn [ BA* ( Eθ* [T]; 1/n ∑_i T_i ) ] MAP: E_Dn [ BA* ( Eθ* [T]; (n0μ0 + ∑_i T_i)/(n0 + n) ) ], where the expectation is on the data Dn = (T1, . . . , Tn).
More explicitly, we want an upper bound that does not involve this expectation over the dataset.
However, we have yet to find a solution encompassing both a broad range of exponential families and applicable to small sample sizes n . d.

artifact.status_search_result: The problem was posed as an open problem in late 2021 on bounding the expected KL/Bregman risk of the MLE and conjugate MAP for exponential families in a non-asymptotic, finite-sample, broad-family manner. No general solution covering both broad exponential families and the small-sample regime appears in subsequent literature; the original posting explicitly notes the absence of such a result, and follow-up work (e.g., on exponential-family KL identities and SMD-type analyses) does not provide a comprehensive resolution.

status_evidence.title: Convergence Rates for the MAP of an Exponential Family and Stochastic Mirror Descent -- an Open Problem
status_evidence.snippet: Considers upper bounding the expected log-likelihood sub-optimality of MLE / conjugate MAP for an exponential family in a non-asymptotic way; no general solution found in the literature, in particular not for Gaussians or few-samples regimes.
status_evidence.claim: The bound is posed as an open problem with no known general solution at time of posting.

status_evidence.title: Exponential families from a single KL identity
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work revisiting KL identities for exponential families; does not provide a general finite-sample upper bound on the expected KL of MLE/MAP across broad families and small n.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent related work does not resolve the open problem in full generality.
